about.description_short: Wintrust is a financial holding company with $74.7 billion in assets whose common stock is traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Guided by its 'Different Approach, Better Results®' philosophy, Wintrust offers the sophisticated resources of a large bank while providing a community banking experience to each customer. Wintrust operates more than 200 retail banking locations through 16 community bank subsidiaries in the greater Chicago, southern Wisconsin, west Michigan, northwest Indiana, and southwest Florida market areas. In addition, Wintrust operates various non-bank business units, providing residential mortgage origination, wealth management, commercial and life insurance premium financing, short-term accounts receivable financing/outsourced administrative services to the temporary staffing services industry, and qualified intermediary services for tax-deferred exchanges.

analysis_md:
# WTFC — Wintrust Financial Corporation
v5 run, 2026-10-20. In scope (market cap $9.671B at $142.44, nasdaq_quote_api). **Finance sector — the OE/capex DCF fits banks poorly; confidence is low by rule, and the final tier is softened one notch from tier-by-numbers under the universal misfit rule — see Final verdict.**

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, statements.json, or the cited search results — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Rosemont, Illinois bank holding company (SIC 6022 State Commercial Banks, fundamentals.json profile): 16 separately branded community-bank charters concentrated in metropolitan Chicago and southern Wisconsin, extended into Indiana and Michigan (Macatawa Bank, closed 3Q24 — its largest merger and first in Michigan, per KBRA via search results), plus specialty finance (insurance premium finance, equipment finance) and wealth management. Founded 1991; growth is organic (de novo branching) plus selective acquisitions paid for partly in stock. Latest prints are a record streak: Q2 2026 was the sixth consecutive quarter of record net income and Q3 2026 the seventh (Q3 2026 release, via search results: net income $239,054,000, EPS $3.37 vs $3.31 consensus, net revenue $757,877,000, net interest income $621,604,000; total assets $75,971,620,000, total loans $56,804,571,000, total deposits $62,435,216,000, CET1 10.5% at September 30, 2026). Q2 2026 (via search results): EPS $3.30, +18.7% YoY, revenue $738,635,000, +10.5% YoY, net interest margin 3.52%, with management citing strong diversified loan growth funded by robust organic deposit growth and guiding to continued net interest income expansion at a stable margin (~3.50% expected range).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $910,348,000; capex $49,951,000 (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment — key_numbers.md capex basis FY2025: $50.0M rollup, PP&E $50.0M + intangibles $0.00); SBC $42,000,000 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, always a real cost — see SBC_TAG_RECONCILED below).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $818,397,000 = $12.05/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $12.05, latest FY OE total $818.4M).
- Maintenance version (financials_history.csv): $840,793,000 — close to the conservative figure; for a bank both definitions are approximations (loan growth, the real "capex" of a bank, is an investing outflow neither captures), which is exactly the sector-mismatch caveat.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt: the engine computes none (net_debt_latest is null — see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK / CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED below).
- History shape (financials_history.csv): conservative OE/share was $10.70 in FY2023, $9.22 in FY2024 and $12.05 in FY2025; the longer series is plumbing-volatile (FY2020 −$9.95/share on negative OCF, FY2022 $21.46/share) while diluted EPS (fundamentals.json) moved steadily — $9.58 / $10.31 / $11.40 over FY2023–FY2025, net income $622,626,000 / $695,045,000 / $823,844,000. The OCF leg, not earnings, is the noisy leg at this bank.
- Earnings cross-check: the median base of $10.70/share sits just below FY2025 diluted EPS of $11.40 (fundamentals.json) — the OCF base is in the same zone as the earnings base here, unlike the gross bank artifacts seen elsewhere in this sweep. That is why the median base is usable (at low confidence) rather than escalated.

**Base used = normalized median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $10.70/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; the median year is FY2023).

**TTM base — attempted, unavailable, and not used.** ttm.py was run and exited 3: "cannot compute TTM for WTFC (CIK 1015328): capex: no post-FY YTD fact (no 10-Q since the 2025-12-31 fiscal year end)" — Wintrust's 10-Qs do not file the capex leg ttm.py needs (fundamentals.json's quarterly rows likewise carry no capex for any 2025–2026 quarter), so no filing-direct TTM OE exists and no --ttm pin was passed. Cross-check from fundamentals.json's TTM block (through Q2 2026): TTM net income $900,359,000 and TTM revenue $2,863,902,000 (+11.5% YoY) confirm the earnings trajectory is above the FY2025 base, while TTM operating cash flow of $1,643,732,000 is unusable as an OE anchor — it is carried by a single $927,183,000 OCF print in Q1 2026 (fundamentals.json quarterly), the usual bank balance-sheet plumbing. The median base stands; the current run-rate is instead reflected, capped, in the scenario growth starts below.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate, high quality for a regional bank
Justification: a scaled Chicago community-bank franchise (16 separately branded charters, 3rd-largest deposit market share in Illinois in 2025 per KBRA via search results; deposits $61,141,275,000 at June 30, 2026) with specialty-finance diversification (FY2025 noninterest income $501,940,000, statements.json) and through-cycle returns (ROE 11.53% / 10.96% / 11.35% in FY2023–FY2025 and ROA 1.11% / 1.07% / 1.16%, fundamentals.json; fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross margin for a bank presentation — both null — so ROE/ROA are the return evidence, as in the UMBF run) — against a commodity banking product with no structural pricing power (NIM 3.52% in Q2 2026 is earned, not owned), full credit- and rate-cycle exposure, regulatory capital limits (CET1 10.4% at June 30, 2026), Chicago/Midwest geographic concentration, and a dilution-funded acquisition model (diluted shares growing 4.2%/yr). An 11%-ish ROE through the recent cycle is above a bank's cost of equity but not the sustained well-above-cost-of-capital record a 7+ moat requires.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-20)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's g_base of 3.94% is not usable as printed. Its revenue components are the growth of the contract-revenue tag (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax), which for a bank captures only a fee slice — the CSV revenue line is $265,635,000 in FY2025 against the bank-basis revenue (net interest income $2,224,052,000 + noninterest income $501,940,000 = $2,725,992,000, statements.json / fundamentals.json) — so rev CAGR 5y 9.32%, rev CAGR 3y 6.85% and latest rev YoY 5.94% describe the wrong series (same defect documented in the HBAN/MTB runs), and the blend then deducts a further −4.15pp share-count adjustment for dilution that has stopped (outstanding count flat through 2026, above) and that was acquisition issuance, not creep. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.119351 / −0.039351 / +0.020649 / +0.060649 / +0.110649 vs g_base) to −8.0 / 0.0 / **+6.0** / +10.0 / +15.0%. Sanity check against prints: bank-basis revenue grew +11.2% in FY2025 and +11.5% YoY on fundamentals.json's TTM block; Q2 2026 revenue +10.5% YoY and EPS +18.7% YoY, Q3 2026 revenue +8.7% YoY (all via search results). Even the super-bull start (+15.0%) sits below the latest EPS print (+18.7%), and the base start (+6.0%) sits below every recent revenue print — with the written reason that those prints are a benign-credit, stable-NIM moment: the FY2025 provision of $95,553,000 is a trough through-cycle cost, and mid-single-digit growth is what a regional bank compounds at once provisions normalize and deposit repricing bites. Management gives no EPS guidance (Q2 2026 release, via search results), so there is no guidance figure to check the starts against; the NII-expansion commentary is consistent with the base case, not the bulls. Probabilities are the defaults 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $142.44.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): ttm.py was run and exited 3 — no post-FY YTD capex fact exists in Wintrust's 10-Qs, so no filing-direct TTM base can be built; its failure and the fundamentals.json TTM cross-check (TTM net income $900,359,000; TTM OCF $1,643,732,000 carried by one $927,183,000 Q1 2026 print) are quoted in the Owner's earnings section. The median base is used, with the current run-rate reflected, capped, in the scenario growth starts.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 4.2%/yr): the growth is acquisition issuance, not SBC creep — diluted shares rose from 62,087,000 in FY2023 to 64,701,000 in FY2024 to 67,894,000 in FY2025 (financials_history.csv) across the Macatawa close (3Q24) and smaller deals, and the count has been flat since (67,465,967 outstanding at July 31, 2026 in dcf_numbers.json; 67,472,459 at September 30, 2026, via search results). SBC itself is rising in dollars but small: $33,500,000 in FY2023, $38,900,000 in FY2024, $42,000,000 in FY2025 (financials_history.csv, Allocated basis) — about 4.6% of FY2025 OCF — and is deducted in full in every OE figure. The engine's −4.15pp growth adjustment was not carried into the scenario starts, for the reasons in the DCF section.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag reports for FY2025 — net debt UNKNOWN, not zero): stated from the filing instead. Balance sheet at FY2025 (financials_history.csv): assets $71,142,046,000, liabilities $63,883,331,000, equity $7,258,715,000; the funding is deposits of $57,717,191,000 (statements.json), against total loans of $53,105,101,000 at December 31, 2025 (Q3 2026 release comparative, via search results). At June 30, 2026 (10-Q, via search results): assets $74,668,135,000, gross loans $55,654,947,000 less allowance for loan losses $402,952,000 = net loans $55,251,995,000, deposits $61,141,275,000 (noninterest-bearing $11,796,736,000 + interest-bearing $49,344,539,000), equity $7,525,116,000. A bank's leverage is its deposit-funded balance sheet and its capital ratios — CET1 10.4% and total capital 12.4% at June 30, 2026 (via search results) — not an industrial net-debt figure; no leverage verdict is taken from the engine.
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED** (the only FY2025 cash tag is the combined cash + restricted-cash total, $467,938,000 in financials_history.csv): accepted — the combined figure cannot be split from the tags, and since the engine computes no net debt for this name at all (DEBT_TAGS_BLANK), no HIGH_NET_DEBT absence is being trusted. The balance sheet is stated from the filing under DEBT_TAGS_BLANK above; the restricted portion is escrow/collateral-type cash a bank holds against client and regulatory obligations, not distributable surplus, and it is given no credit in the verdict.
- **SBC_TAG_RECONCILED** (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense exceeds ShareBasedCompensation in FY2017 +0.3%, FY2018 +0.0%, FY2020 +-0.8%, FY2021 +0.1%, FY2023 +0.0%, FY2024 +2.1%, FY2025 +1.1%; the Allocated figure was used): confirmed — the differences in the three base years are +0.0% (FY2023), +2.1% (FY2024: $38,900,000 vs $38,108,000) and +1.1% (FY2025: $42,000,000 vs $41,551,000), i.e. the Share tag carries only part of stock compensation and the larger Allocated figure the engine used is the conservative one; the FY2024/FY2025 gaps are above the 1% rounding line but in the direction that lowers OE, so the base is not flattered by the choice.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance): accepted in full. A bank's OCF-based "owner's earnings" are not its distributable cash — loan growth consumes regulatory capital, provisions are a through-cycle cost the OCF line adds back, and bank value is normally judged on ROE vs cost of equity and tangible book, none of which this model computes. The cross-checks: FY2025 book value per share $106.91 (fundamentals.json) puts the $142.44 price at 1.33x book; tangible book value per share was $92.13 at June 30, 2026 (via search results), 1.55x at the price, for a franchise earning an 11.35% ROE in FY2025. Confidence is low, and the final tier is softened one notch under the universal rule (see Final verdict).
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.33x): real — a bank's outcome range across a credit cycle IS wide (super-bear IV@15% $42.40 vs super-bull $183.64). Confidence is low (also mandated by the sector flag), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear-case tier D at 8.65% vs bull-case tier C at 14.12%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — the final tier (D, after the misfit softening) equals the bear-case tier.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The method range is narrow for once: the preliminary default run (median base, engine growth starts) printed Tier C at a weighted IRR of 11.36% (IV@15% $99.78), and the final recalibrated run prints Tier C at 11.73% ($103.76). Both sit below the 15% hurdle, and the bear case is D on either. The disagreement is not about the franchise — it is executing at a record level — but about what a buyer should pay for bank earnings photographed at a benign credit moment.
- Quality is not the debate: 16 charters, #3 deposit share in Illinois, a 53.4% efficiency ratio (Q3 2026, via search results), ROE holding 11.0–11.5% through FY2023–FY2025, and seven straight record net-income quarters. The debate is price and cycle position: at $142.44 the buyer pays 1.55x the June 30, 2026 tangible book value per share of $92.13 (via search results) — a full price for an ~11% ROE — while the loan book ($55,654,947,000 at June 30, 2026) has been grown into the benign stretch and the FY2025 provision of $95,553,000 is a trough cost.
- Bank-specific cross-check the model cannot do: if through-cycle ROE settles near the FY2023–FY2025 level (~11%), the earnings power is roughly the current one and the base case here is fair; the stock's return from $142.44 then comes from growth plus the $2.00 FY2025 dividend per share, not from a re-rating — which is exactly what an 11.73% weighted IRR says.
- Price that clears 15%: the weighted IV@15% is $103.76 — the stock clears Andrew's hurdle at or below that level on the numbers, before the misfit softening and before any additional margin of safety. Note Q3 2026 tangible book value per share printed $88.18 (via search results), down from $92.13 at Q2 — worth watching, but it does not change any figure the score rests on.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (tier_override from tier-by-numbers C: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH universal softening, Andrew's standing rule 2026-10-15 made universal 2026-10-19 — a bank's OCF-based OE is not distributable earnings: loan growth consumes regulatory capital (loans grew from $53,105,101,000 at FY2025 year-end to $55,654,947,000 at June 30, 2026) and the provision for credit losses is a through-cycle cost OCF adds back ($95,553,000 in FY2025), photographed in a benign credit window (seven consecutive record net-income quarters through Q3 2026); the numbers tier C at 11.73% already sits below the hurdle and the bear case prints D at 8.65%)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector-model mismatch plus a 4.33x scenario spread; the filing data itself is complete — no data gaps, no field overrides; the TTM base is unavailable because the 10-Qs file no capex leg)
- One-liner: High-quality Chicago community-bank franchise (16 charters, seven straight record net-income quarters), moat 5/10 — median OE $10.70/sh is a 7.51% yield at $142.44, but weighted IRR is only 11.73% (IV@15% $103.76), Tier C by numbers and softened to D under the universal bank-misfit notch; it clears 15% only below ~$104; confidence low.
